mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.5% signals accelerating economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 rises above 2.5% for 6 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 95% of its 12-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO falls below 95% of its 12-month moving average for 3 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for 3 months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.
